subject: ela
cluster: Research to build and present knowledge
skillName: Gather relevant information from multiple sources
intro: Practice gathering information for research. For each item you will pick the relevant source, judge whether a source is credible, spot a word-for-word copy, or find the missing citation part. Everything you need is in the item itself.

items.prompt:
Research question: How do plants make their own food? Which source title is most relevant to this question?
A) Photosynthesis: How Plants Make Food (a science textbook chapter)
B) Best Flowers to Plant in Spring (a gardening blog)
C) Funny Plant Memes (a humor website)
D) How to Build a Wooden Planter Box (a craft site)
items.answer: A) Photosynthesis: How Plants Make Food (a science textbook chapter)

steps: The research question asks how plants make their own food.
Source A is about photosynthesis, which is exactly the process plants use to make food, so it directly answers the question.
B, C, and D all mention plants but cover spring flowers, jokes, and building a box, none of which explain how plants make food, so they are off topic.

items.prompt:
Research question: Is the water at City Beach safe to swim in this week? Which source is more credible?
A) A report posted this week on the County Health Department website (.gov) listing this week's water test results
B) A comment on a social media post from a user who wrote: I think it is fine, I swam there last summer
C) An ad for swimsuits that says City Beach is the place to be
D) A photo someone posted of the beach with no information about the water
items.answer: A) A report posted this week on the County Health Department website (.gov) listing this week's water test results

steps: A credible source comes from an expert, is recent, and offers real evidence.
Source A is from a health department (expert), is from this week (recent), and gives water test results (evidence), so it is the most credible.
B is one person's opinion from last summer, C is an ad trying to sell swimsuits, and D is just a photo with no water information, so none of them are reliable for this question.

items.prompt:
A student is researching the planets. Read the original source sentence: 'Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.' Which student version is plagiarism because it copies the sentence word for word with no quotation marks and no credit?
A) Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
B) According to NASA, Jupiter is the biggest of all the planets that orbit the sun.
C) Of all the planets that circle the sun, Jupiter is the largest one.
D) The source explains that no planet in our solar system is bigger than Jupiter.
items.answer: A) Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.

steps: Plagiarism includes copying a sentence exactly without quotation marks and without crediting the source.
Version A repeats the original sentence word for word with no quotation marks and no credit, so it is plagiarism.
B, C, and D restate the idea in the student's own words or credit the source, so they are acceptable.

items.prompt:
Read this citation: 'Saving the Bees. Nature Now. 2021.' A complete citation needs author, title, source or website name, and date. Which element is missing from this citation?
A) The author
B) The title
C) The source or website name
D) The date

steps: A basic citation needs four parts: author, title, source or website name, and date.
This citation gives the title (Saving the Bees), the source (Nature Now), and the date (2021).
There is no author listed, so the author is the missing element. The other parts are present, so B, C, and D are wrong.

items.prompt:
Research question: What did people eat in ancient Rome? Which source title is most relevant?
A) Food and Meals in Ancient Rome (a history museum web page)
B) Top Pizza Restaurants in Rome Today (a travel blog)
C) Learn to Speak Modern Italian (a language site)
D) Cheap Flights to Rome This Summer (a travel ad)
items.answer: A) Food and Meals in Ancient Rome (a history museum web page)

steps: The question asks what people ate in ancient Rome.
Source A is specifically about food and meals in ancient Rome, so it directly answers the question.
B is about restaurants today, C is about learning Italian, and D is a flight ad, so they do not answer what ancient Romans ate.

items.prompt:
Research question: How fast can a cheetah run? Which source is more credible?
A) An article on a wildlife conservation organization's website that cites speed measurements from scientists
B) A quick reply on a message board where a user wrote: pretty sure it is super fast
items.answer: A) An article on a wildlife conservation organization's website that cites speed measurements from scientists

steps: Credible sources come from experts and offer evidence.
Source A is from a wildlife organization and reports measurements from scientists, which is expert evidence.
Source B is one user's vague guess with no evidence, so it is not credible.

items.prompt:
Read the original source sentence: 'The Great Wall of China is thousands of miles long.' Which student version is a word-for-word copy with no quotation marks and no credit, making it plagiarism?
A) The Great Wall of China is thousands of miles long.
B) The Great Wall of China stretches for thousands of miles, the book notes.
C) Spanning thousands of miles, the Great Wall of China is extremely long.
D) One source reports that the Great Wall runs for many thousands of miles.
items.answer: A) The Great Wall of China is thousands of miles long.

steps: Copying a sentence exactly without quotation marks or credit is plagiarism.
Version A is identical to the original sentence with no quotation marks and no source, so it is plagiarism.
B credits the book, and C and D reword the idea, so they are not plagiarism.

items.prompt:
Read this citation: '"The Water Cycle." Science Kids. 2020.' A complete citation needs author, title, source or website name, and date. Which element is missing?
A) The author
B) The title
C) The source or website name
D) The date

steps: A basic citation needs author, title, source or website name, and date.
This citation has the title (The Water Cycle), the source (Science Kids), and the date (2020).
No author is named, so the author is missing. The other elements are present, so B, C, and D are incorrect.

items.prompt:
Research question: Why do leaves change color in the fall? Which source title is most relevant?
A) Why Leaves Change Color in Autumn (a university biology page)
B) Crafts to Make With Fallen Leaves (a kids' activity blog)
C) Best Hiking Trails for Fall Views (a travel site)
D) Buy Fake Autumn Leaves for Decorating (a store ad)
items.answer: A) Why Leaves Change Color in Autumn (a university biology page)

steps: The question asks why leaves change color in the fall.
Source A directly explains why leaves change color in autumn, so it answers the question.
B, C, and D mention leaves or fall but cover crafts, hiking, and shopping, so they do not explain the color change.

items.prompt:
Research question: How many bones are in the human body? Which source is more credible?
A) A page on a children's hospital website (.org) written by doctors
B) An ad for a vitamin that claims it makes your bones the strongest ever
items.answer: A) A page on a children's hospital website (.org) written by doctors

steps: A credible source comes from experts and aims to inform, not to sell.
Source A is written by doctors on a hospital website, so it is an expert source meant to inform.
Source B is an ad whose purpose is to sell a vitamin, so it is not a reliable source for facts about bones.

items.prompt:
Read the original source sentence: 'Honeybees pollinate many of the crops that farmers grow.' Which student version is plagiarism because it copies the sentence exactly without quotation marks or credit?
A) Honeybees pollinate many of the crops that farmers grow.
B) The article states that honeybees help pollinate many farm crops.
C) Many crops grown by farmers are pollinated by honeybees, according to the source.
D) Honeybees play a big role in pollinating the crops farmers depend on, the report says.
items.answer: A) Honeybees pollinate many of the crops that farmers grow.

steps: An exact copy with no quotation marks and no credit is plagiarism.
Version A repeats the original sentence word for word with nothing crediting the source, so it is plagiarism.
B, C, and D credit the source or reword the idea, so they are acceptable.

items.prompt:
Read this citation: 'Carlos Reyes. Volcanoes and How They Erupt. 2019.' A complete citation needs author, title, source or website name, and date. Which element is missing?
A) The source or website name
B) The author
C) The title
D) The date
items.answer: A) The source or website name

steps: A basic citation needs author, title, source or website name, and date.
This citation lists the author (Carlos Reyes), the title (Volcanoes and How They Erupt), and the date (2019).
It does not name the source or website where the work was published, so that element is missing. The author, title, and date are present, so B, C, and D are wrong.

B) The History of the Cereal Box (a packaging blog)
C) Funniest Breakfast Fails on Video (an entertainment site)
D) Win a Free Toaster: Enter Now (a contest ad)
items.answer: A) Healthy Breakfast Ideas for Children (a pediatric nutrition guide)

B, C, and D mention breakfast topics but cover packaging history, funny videos, and a contest, so they are off topic.

items.prompt:
Research question: When was the first airplane flight? Which source is more credible?
A) An article on a national air and space museum website (.gov) that lists the date and historical records
B) A personal blog post titled My Opinion on Old Planes with no facts or sources listed
items.answer: A) An article on a national air and space museum website (.gov) that lists the date and historical records

steps: A credible source is an expert source that offers evidence such as records or dates.
Source A is from a museum and provides the date and historical records, so it is expert and evidence based.
Source B is one person's opinion with no facts or sources, so it is not credible for this question.

items.prompt:
Read the original source sentence: 'Sea turtles travel thousands of miles to lay their eggs on the same beach.' Which student version is plagiarism because it copies the sentence word for word with no quotation marks and no credit?
A) Sea turtles travel thousands of miles to lay their eggs on the same beach.
B) The book says sea turtles swim thousands of miles back to the same beach to nest.
C) To lay their eggs, sea turtles return to one beach after traveling thousands of miles, the source notes.
D) Sea turtles journey great distances so they can nest on the beach where they were born, according to the article.
items.answer: A) Sea turtles travel thousands of miles to lay their eggs on the same beach.

steps: Copying a sentence exactly with no quotation marks and no credit is plagiarism.
Version A matches the original sentence word for word with nothing crediting the source, so it is plagiarism.
B, C, and D credit the source and reword the idea, so they are not plagiarism.
